facts.text: Pilot studies test feasibility rather than effectiveness, according to Thabane and colleagues (2010). This evidence comes from health and social research rather than heavy-machine virtual testing.
facts.quote: Pilot studies test feasibility, not effectiveness (Thabane and colleagues, 2010)

facts.text: Pilot studies should not be used to estimate effect sizes, according to Leon, Davis and Kraemer (2011). This recommendation comes from health and social research.
facts.quote: should not be used to estimate effect sizes (Leon, Davis and Kraemer, 2011)

facts.text: The CONSORT extension for pilot and feasibility trials (Eldridge and colleagues, 2016) and work on progression criteria by Avery and colleagues (2017, traffic-light criteria) and Mellor and colleagues (2023) support stating progression criteria before results are known.

facts.text: Registered Reports were rated higher on rigour than conventional papers in the work of Soderberg and colleagues (2021), in health and social research.

facts.text: Pre-registration (Nosek and colleagues, 2018) and Registered Reports support locking metrics in advance; this support comes from health and social research.
facts.quote: Pre-registration (Nosek and colleagues, 2018) and Registered Reports, which were rated higher on rigour than conventional papers (Soderberg and colleagues, 2021), support locking metrics in advance

facts.text: Transferring the health and social research literature on pilots, progression criteria and pre-registration to engineering is a supporting analogy rather than direct proof.

facts.quote: Building-block validation (AIAA, 1998; Oberkampf and Roy, 2010)

facts.text: Blind prediction as used in the Sandia Fracture Challenges is an engineering analogue for a pilot or proof of concept.
facts.quote: blind prediction as in the Sandia Fracture Challenges

facts.text: A walking skeleton exercises the whole toolchain end to end at low fidelity and is an engineering analogue for a pilot or proof of concept.
facts.quote: a "walking skeleton" that exercises the whole toolchain end to end at low fidelity

facts.text: DARPA and ARPA-E phase metrics are engineering analogues for scoping and assessing a pilot or proof of concept.
facts.quote: DARPA and ARPA-E phase metrics

facts.text: The validation envelope versus intended-use domain in NATM and NASA-STD-7009B provides an engineering analogue for a pilot or proof of concept.
facts.quote: the validation envelope versus intended-use domain of NATM and NASA-STD-7009B

facts.text: The FDA's Software Precertification pilot ran from 2017 to September 2022.
facts.quote: The FDA's Software Precertification pilot (2017 to September 2022)

facts.text: The FDA's Software Precertification pilot did not validate its original concept but produced findings about what could and could not be done under the existing framework.
facts.quote: a pilot that did not validate its original concept and still produced findings about what could and could not be done under the existing framework

facts.text: A pilot does not have to succeed to be useful, as illustrated by the FDA's Software Precertification pilot.
facts.quote: a pilot does not have to "succeed" to be useful

facts.text: A virtual-validation pilot should be a deliberately difficult thin vertical slice rather than an attractive demonstration: one safety function, one or two machine variants, representative normal cases plus boundary, degraded and known-difficult cases, an end-to-end model and toolchain, physical or bench comparators, and pre-declared go, restricted-go, pivot and stop criteria. Low visibility or an occluded person are examples of known-difficult cases.
facts.quote: one safety function, one or two machine variants, representative normal cases plus boundary, degraded and known-difficult cases (for example low visibility or an occluded person), an end-to-end model and toolchain, physical or bench comparators, and pre-declared go, restricted-go, pivot and stop criteria

facts.text: A concrete recommended virtual-validation pilot runs in months 3 to 5.
facts.quote: run it in months 3 to 5

facts.text: A concrete recommended virtual-validation pilot uses 3 to 5 scenario classes, including at least one edge case.
facts.quote: choose 3 to 5 scenario classes including at least one edge case

facts.text: A concrete recommended virtual-validation pilot pre-specifies 10 to 30 physical test points.
facts.quote: pre-specify 10 to 30 physical test points

facts.text: A virtual-validation pilot should simulate blind before the physical results are seen.
facts.quote: simulate blind before the physical results are seen

facts.text: A virtual-validation pilot should compare results against pre-registered metrics such as detection-range error, stopping-distance error and false-negative agreement.
facts.quote: compare against pre-registered metrics such as detection-range error, stopping-distance error and false-negative agreement

facts.text: A virtual-validation pilot should report results as a traffic light showing the trusted envelope and the failures.
facts.quote: report as a traffic light that shows the trusted envelope and the failures

facts.text: A polished animation of one nominal cycle has almost no evidentiary value for a virtual-validation pilot.
facts.quote: A polished animation of one nominal cycle has almost no evidentiary value.

facts.text: A pilot charter should identify the larger decision that the pilot evidence will inform, making the pilot auditable before it starts.
facts.quote: | Decision | What larger decision will the pilot evidence inform? |

facts.text: A pilot charter should state what is genuinely unknown before the pilot starts.
facts.quote: | Uncertainty | What do we genuinely not know? |

facts.text: A pilot charter should scope one function, configuration and envelope, with explicit exclusions.
facts.quote: | Scope | One function, configuration and envelope, with explicit exclusions |

facts.text: A pilot charter should specify the end-to-end chain: stimulus, model or system, safety response, measurement and verdict.
facts.quote: | End-to-end chain | Stimulus, model or system, safety response, measurement, verdict |

facts.text: A pilot charter should identify a comparator, such as a bench, physical machine, field record, independent model or analytical truth.
facts.quote: | Comparator | Bench, physical machine, field record, independent model or analytical truth |

facts.text: A pilot charter should specify normal, boundary, degraded and known difficult or failure challenge cases.
facts.quote: | Challenge cases | Normal, boundary, degraded and known difficult or failure cases |

facts.text: A pilot charter should specify metrics for accuracy, timing, reproducibility, coverage, failure detection and effort.
facts.quote: | Metrics | Accuracy, timing, reproducibility, coverage, failure detection, effort |

facts.text: A pilot charter should specify progression criteria for go, restricted go, pivot and stop.
facts.quote: | Progression criteria | Go, restricted go, pivot, stop |

facts.text: A pilot charter should specify what discrepancy is acceptable and why, as its credibility criteria.
facts.quote: | Credibility criteria | What discrepancy is acceptable, and why? |

facts.text: A pilot charter should state the residual uncertainty that will remain even after success.
facts.quote: | Residual uncertainty | What remains unknown even after success? |

facts.text: A pilot charter should specify deliverables consisting of raw data, results, a discrepancy log, a credibility report and repeatable scripts.
facts.quote: | Deliverables | Raw data, results, discrepancy log, credibility report, repeatable scripts |

facts.text: A pilot charter should state exactly what the pilot does not establish, as its claim limit.
facts.quote: | Claim limit | Exactly what the pilot does not establish |

facts.text: A credible pilot conclusion should bound model-to-test agreement by operating regimes, configuration, pre-agreed tolerances and metrics, and explicitly identify failed criteria and conditions. The example reports agreement for metrics X and Y within three operating regimes on configuration A, but failure of criterion Z in condition Q.
facts.quote: Within these three operating regimes, on configuration A, model-to-test discrepancy remained within the pre-agreed tolerance for metrics X and Y; the simulation failed criterion Z in condition Q.

facts.text: A delivery programme should limit virtual-evidence claims to the metrics supported by the pilot and retain physical confirmation for conditions where the simulation failed. In the example, virtual evidence is claimed for X and Y only, while condition Q retains physical confirmation.
facts.quote: The delivery programme will therefore claim virtual evidence for X and Y only, while Q retains physical confirmation.

facts.text: A bounded pilot conclusion that states agreement, failures and limits on virtual-evidence claims is far stronger than saying only that the proof of concept was successful.
facts.quote: That is far stronger than "the proof of concept was successful".
